item: ooLive: one shared helper for text drawn in the active language that follows a language switch (row 364, for the row 352 list)
summary: ooLive(el, render) draws render() as text into one inner span marked data-i18n-dyn and leaves el itself unmarked, so a button's own translated title keeps following the walker; ooLiveHtml(el, render) marks el, since its markup is the render's. Both keep render; ooLiveRepaint, called once from the oo:langchange listener, redraws every kept node in the new language and never fetches. ooLive(el, null) releases el: the marker goes unless the page put it there, and the nodes el held before come back, so a button's static label returns to the walker, which still knows its English. A node gone from the page is dropped (on repaint and on the next draw), a node something else wrote since its last draw is dropped and left as it is, and a render that throws is caught for its node alone. The row 352 scanner blanks the arguments of an ooLive/ooLiveHtml call before matching sinks and translators, so only the node passed is exempt: a write to another node, to the same node outside the call, or after a release still counts (fixtures for each). The node test runs the shipped helper with the shipped t() and the shipped walker doText()/tr(), and every mutation of the helper fails it but one that only redraws the span when it need not (behaviour-equivalent). A write by other code that leaves the same text but replaces the span is also dropped. The Opus read found two defects, both fixed before the PR: a foreign write was told by comparing innerHTML, which the hover convention changes when it marks a [title], so every titled HTML node would have been dropped at the first switch (the text is now the fingerprint); and an inline render that wrote another node was blanked with the call (a call whose arguments hold a sink is now counted as ordinary code). No list line changes in this PR; the row 361 fixes use it and delete their own lines.
